title: The Spirit in the Glass Bottle (Der Geist im Glas)

keywords: the spirit in the glass bottle (der geist im glas)
full_text:
A poor woodcutter worked from morning till evening to save enough money to send his only son to school. The lad was clever and learned diligently, but before he could complete his studies, his father's meager savings ran out, and the youth returned home to chop timber in the forest.

One afternoon, while resting beneath a colossal ancient oak tree, the boy heard a muffled, trembling voice calling from beneath the roots: "Let me out! Let me out!" Digging into the moss, he uncovered a sealed glass flagon. He uncorked the bottle, and instantly a thick column of dark smoke poured out, condensing into a gigantic, terrifying spirit that towered over the trees.

"I am Mercurius!" roared the demon. "I have been locked in this bottle for centuries, and my reward to whoever releases me is to snap his neck!"

The lad did not tremble. With supreme composure, he smiled and said, "Before I let you snap my neck, prove to me that you truly came from that tiny flagon! A titan of your vast stature could never have fit inside."

"You doubt my greatness?" roared the vain spirit. Shrinking himself into a thin vapor, the demon poured himself entirely back into the bottle to demonstrate his power. In a flash, the boy jammed the cork tightly back into the neck, trapping the spirit once again.

Realizing he had been outsmarted, the spirit begged for mercy, promising the boy an enchanted rag that could heal any wound and turn plain iron into pure silver. The boy accepted the treasure and freed the spirit. With the magical cloth, the youth turned his rusty axe into silver, paid for his medical studies, and became the most renowned physician in the realm, celebrated for both his brilliant mind and his miraculous healing touch.
moral: Sharp intellect and presence of mind can outwit ancient magic and turn peril into lasting prosperity.
